newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco credit firm Eqdom capital up 50pct.
newsitem.headline: Morocco credit firm Eqdom capital up 50pct.

text.p: Morocco's main consumer credit firm Eqdom has increased its capital by more than 50.3 percent to 167.02 million dirhams ($18.9 million), its chairman said on Thursday.
"This capital increase came in the view of promising prospects," Eqdom director, Abdellatif Abenouas, said in a news conference.
Eqdom controls 33 percent of the country's credit consumer market except for the car part of the market, through its 1,400 retailers and agencies network.
Eqdom registered a net profit of 76.3 million dirhams ($8.7 million) for the first half of 1996 compared with 53.4 million dirhams in the same period in 1995, according to the latest available data.
Eqdom, Morocco's first consumer credit company, was set up in 1974 by holding company Societe Nationale d'Investissment and major insurance firms.
Eqdom, which is listed on the Casblanca Bourse, last traded on Thursday at 857 dirhams against 832 dirhams on Wednesday. ($1=8.8 dirhams)
